sn11.10:1.2: This opening is reminiscent of [ud1.10](), which specifies the location as Suppāraka
sn11.10:1.7: A barbarian (_dāsa_) who “fancied himself godlike” (Rig Veda 7.18.20), Śambara’s 99 mountain forts were destroyed for their bounty (6.47.23) by Indra on behalf of Divodāsa Atithigva (4.26.3). His mention close to Virocana here (sn11.8]() fits the Arthaśāstra, where they are both invoked together (14.3.19; see [sn11.23]()). Despite his decisive defeat at the hands of Indra, later legend makes him a formidable foe and master of sorcery.
